An OpenTofu (Terraform) plan is about to be applied to live infrastructure on one server: Docker containers and volumes, and a PostgreSQL server whose databases are used by running applications. Applying the plan carries out the resource changes below in dependency order. Replacing a resource destroys the old one and then creates the new one, unless the plan says the new one is created first (create_before_destroy). If a change fails, the apply stops there; the changes already made stay made.

Current state:
postgresql_database.app: database s44_app owned by s44_app; open sessions: 1 as role s44_app; tables: public.app_t (1,000 rows, owner s44_app)
postgresql_role.app: role s44_app, can log in, has a password; open sessions: 1 in database s44_app

Actions, in order:
1. Update postgresql_database.app in place: owner: "s44_app" -> "s44_admin"
2. Create postgresql_role.admin: name = "s44_admin"; login = false

How these providers behave: Destroying a postgresql_database drops the database with everything stored in it; PostgreSQL refuses to drop or rename a database while other sessions are connected to it, and the change fails. Clients log in with a role's name and password: after a role is renamed, gets a new password, or has login = false, new connections with the old name or password fail; sessions already open stay open.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
